poem.content:
In the mesh of city streets, a sudden spray
Of rain awakens the outside world's gray
The misery of umbrellas, a rack to bear
A fleeting comfort, soon to leave us bare

A cute, forgotten boat, a relic of the past
Lies still, a testament to memories that won't last
A fringe of seaweed clings to its wooden frame
A poignant reminder of the grief that's to come

In this desolate scene, a six-legged creature crawls
A tiny, desperate inmate, lost in a world that's cold
It seeks to grow, to find its place in this vast space
But the rack of time and fate holds it in a desperate pace

The tent of life, once a sanctuary, now a cage
A prison of our deepest fears, where we turn the page
To cram the darkness, to silence the pain
But the mesh of our minds, a fragile, frayed refrain

In this world of wonder, where the spray of life is strong
We must learn to destroy the shackles that hold us wrong
To grow, to rise, to find our place in the sun's warm light
And leave the misery of the past to wither in the night.
